title: (c) Existence/uniqueness of the principal eigenpair on ℝ requires confinement hypotheses (Krein–Rutman setup)

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Open sub-lemma, part (c).** The claim of a principal eigenpair $(\lambda,F)$, $F\ge0$, $\int F=1$, for *general smooth* $\beta,\mu$ on the **unbounded** domain $\mathbb R$ is false without confinement. After conjugation $F=e^{(a/D)x}u$ the symmetrized operator is $-\tfrac D2 u'' + V_{\mathrm{eff}}u=\lambda u$ with $V_{\mathrm{eff}}=\mu-\beta+\tfrac{a^2}{2D}$ (signs subject to G1). If $V_{\mathrm{eff}}$ does not grow at $\pm\infty$ the operator has continuous spectrum and no $L^1$-normalizable principal $F$.

**Required:** (i) state the function space / weight; (ii) state and use a confinement hypothesis (e.g. $\mu-\beta\to+\infty$, or $\beta-\mu$ coercive) ensuring discrete bottom spectrum and compact resolvent; (iii) apply Krein–Rutman (positivity, irreducibility) to obtain a simple, dominant, real $\lambda$ with $F>0$; (iv) verify hypotheses of the cited theorem explicitly. Reference: Perthame, *Transport Equations in Biology*.
